chair.lede: We move the clock one second closer, driven chiefly by escalating climate disasters in Syria and Australia combined with a worsening Ebola toll.
body: Severe flooding in eastern Syria killed five children, underscoring an acute humanitarian crisis, while extreme storm warnings across major Australian cities signal a broader intensification of climate risks.
The Congo Ebola outbreak has now exceeded 5,000 deaths, confirming the bio‑risk trajectory highlighted yesterday and adding further pressure on regional stability.
Additionally, OpenAI’s $10 billion funding cut highlights growing economic and governance strains in AI development, compounding the overall risk landscape.

experts.say: Patriot missile sales to Ukraine continue (1,6,15,20) but Iran’s NPT withdrawal calls raise concern (11); overall no clear shift in nuclear risk.
Severe flooding in eastern Syria killed children [2] and intense storm warnings across major Australian cities signal worsening extreme weather events [7].
The Congo Ebola outbreak has surpassed 5,000 deaths, indicating a worsening public health crisis and heightened risk of regional spread [3][8][12].

OpenAI’s move to limit weapons info for teens and its $10 billion funding cut signal heightened concern over AI misuse, while the Pope’s call for ethical frameworks underscores ongoing governance gaps. North Korean hacker activity further highlights cyber‑risk. [4,9,19,23]

US approval of a $2.1 bn Patriot missile sale to Ukraine heightens Russia‑Ukraine tensions, while Iran lawmakers urging NPT withdrawal and tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz raise nuclear and regional risks. (cites 1,11,25)
